name: Crystal-butted wand
description: A slender carved wooden wand with a leather-wrapped grip and two brass bands. A pale blue crystal glows in a brass collar at its butt end.
notes: 380 mm long, 16 mm across at the butt. The reference gives every spell and strength the same look, mass and volume, so all 24 wands share this model; which spell it casts and its charges are left to the magic framework. CHECK VOLUME is not flagged; the model's box is a third of the reference's 500 ml, which reads as the wand's stowed space.

name: Ever-burning wall sconce
description: An oak wall plate bound in iron, with a braced iron arm holding a carved wooden torch. The torch burns with a steady, smokeless flame that never goes out.
notes: 120 mm wide, 170 mm deep and 580 mm tall. CHECK VOLUME (x5.5): the reference 2.25 L is the wood and iron, not the open box round a torch standing out from its plate. It is a fixture to mount on a wall; the light and mounting are left to the light and furniture frameworks. The flame uses glow-flame and the torch head cloth-charred.

name: Iridescent felt patch
description: A small square of thick felt that shifts colour as it turns, with a line of stitching along one edge and a frayed corner. It can be picked apart for its fibre.
notes: 50 by 40 mm and 3 mm thick, `iridescent` felt crossed by diagonal bands of `jelly-teal` and `cloth-purple` where the sheen shifts hue, since no single finish shows a colour shift on a tile. The name drops the reference's fibre name, which belongs to the mod's lore. Disassembling it for fibre is left to the crafting framework.

name: Glowing mushroom strips
description: A handful of slim pale strips cut from a mushroom cap, a teal skin along one edge. A faint blue light still clings to their cut faces.
notes: Six strips about 90 by 14 by 6 mm, heaped 92 by 68 mm and 20 mm tall. The flesh uses jelly-pale and the skin jelly-teal so the strips read moist and translucent; the glow is crystal-glow-blue. Nutrition and its magical effect are left to the food framework.

name: Horn moss capsules
description: Three pure white seed capsules shaped like small blunt horns, tied in a bundle with twine, each plugged at its open end with green moss.
notes: Three round horn tubes 60 mm long and 16 mm across, each with a blunt closed tip and a moss plug in its open end, tied in a bundle with a jute band; the bundle is 62 by 38 by 36 mm. Box/volume x1.7, no flag. Their spores as a reagent and the healing when eaten are left to the crafting and food frameworks. enamel-white draws the pure white shell.

name: Gnarled wooden chair
description: A chair that looks grown rather than built, all of one twisted piece of oak. Its legs kink and flare into roots, and knotted branches cross between the back posts.
notes: 500 mm wide, 520 mm deep and 980 mm tall, the seat 450 mm up. rest matches the wooden chair in earlier drafts; the reference calls it very comfortable, so it could rate higher once rest is tuned. CHECK VOLUME (x8.7): an open chair fills little of its bounding box; the reference's 30 L is its displaced volume. At 12 kg it is furniture to carry across a room; the size is a placeholder.

name: Ever-burning torch stand
description: A homemade oak stand on a crossed foot, its iron-braced arms holding five carved wooden torches. Each burns with a steady, smokeless flame that never goes out.
notes: 800 mm across the arms and 1.51 m tall. CHECK VOLUME (x4.8): the reference 200 L is what the stand displaces, not the open box round its arms. This is furniture to set up in a room; the light is left to the light framework and the size is a placeholder. The torches share the wall sconce's torch shape.

name: Orrery
description: A tabletop model of the planets: a brass sun on a steel column above a walnut plinth, with six planets on arms of different reach round it, one ringed. A crank on the plinth turns the gears that set them moving.
notes: 700 mm across its arms as drawn, 550 mm tall and 360 mm across the plinth; the reference's 800 mm longest side is met with the arms swung apart. CHECK VOLUME (x11.2): the arms enclose mostly empty space; the reference's 20 L is what the orrery displaces. A decoration to set up; the turning crank has no content field yet, and the size is a placeholder.
